proposedBy.onBehalfOf: the owner (KineTrak), on their request to review and propose

statement: Answer "what does changing this touch" in the feature panel (variant a-panel), with the canvas outlining the same items in sync, the list grouped by how directly each is touched (taken from c-ask), and a link into Swimlane with the downstream zone lit. The panel opens beside the selected node, never over it.

evidence.what: server/mcp.ts:385 — no UI surface calls compute_impact; a human cannot ask the question the product exists to answer

keystroke-level estimate from a feature on screen to the answer (Card, Moran & Newell operators): a-panel 2.65 s (point, click, mental) · b-canvas 3.95 s (adds a second point-and-click to enter the mode) · c-ask about 4.4 s (open, type ~10 characters, choose) — a-panel is the shortest because the answer appears where the person already looks

side panels keep the visual connection between the detail and the main view; dialogs interrupt and are wrong for decisions that need other information on screen (NN/g, via design-system guidance) — c-ask is a dialog over the board it is about

dependency tools put relations in the detail side panel (Linear: Blocks / Blocked by in the issue panel) and synchronise graph and list views for impact (Cambridge Intelligence impact analysis; Grafana knowledge graph)
Shneiderman, The Eyes Have It (1996): overview first, zoom and filter, then details on demand — the canvas keeps the overview, the panel holds the details
on the current build the panel covers the node just selected (scratch screenshot detail.png); a panel answer must keep its feature in view
